group: q|what percentage of adults have a university degree worldwide top 1% country

result.why: The question asks for a share of adults (the percentage holding a university degree), either worldwide or in the highest-ranked country. That is a single proportion per country. It is not a distribution of individual values that can be read at the 50th, 90th, 99th or 99.9th percentile. 'Top 1% country' would mean ranking about 190 countries by their tertiary attainment rate and taking the 99th percentile of that country list. The site's grid places a person within a population of people, not a country within a list of countries, so there is no triple that fits the schema without changing what was asked. Sources do exist for the underlying figure: the UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS) educational attainment series (population 25+ who completed at least a bachelor's or equivalent, ISCED 6+), the World Bank WDI indicator SE.TER.CUAT.BA.ZS, which republishes UIS, and OECD Education at a Glance (25-64 year olds with tertiary education). These give one percentage per country, and coverage is incomplete for low-income countries, so a worldwide adult share would be a modelled estimate rather than a published figure. The closest individual-level measure in the catalogue is schooling_years, the years of schooling completed by adults. Rephrased as 'how many years of schooling puts an adult in the top 1% worldwide', it could be researched under that id, but that is a different question from the one asked, so I am not substituting it here.
